'''Jana Zaumseil''' (born 1977) is a [[Germans|German]] [[chemist]] who is a professor of [[physical chemistry]] at [[Heidelberg University]]. She serves as dean of the faculty of chemistry and earth sciences. Her research considers organic electronic materials for optoelectronics.

== Early life and education ==
Zaumseil was born in [[Jena]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Jana Zaumseil erhält Alfried-Krupp-Förderpreis 2010 |url=https://idw-online.de/de/news376323 |access-date=2022-12-08 |website=idw-online.de}}</ref> and studied chemistry at [[Leipzig University]].{{cn|date=December 2022}} After earning her undergraduate degree, she joined [[Bell Labs]]<ref name=":0" /> and spent a year in [[Murray Hill, Manhattan]], before moving to the [[Cavendish Laboratory]].{{cn|date=December 2022}} Zaumseil earned her doctorate at the [[University of Cambridge]], where she worked with [[Henning Sirringhaus]] on ambipolar organic field effect transistors.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Zaumseil |first1=Jana |last2=Sirringhaus |first2=Henning |date=2007-04-01 |title=Electron and Ambipolar Transport in Organic Field-Effect Transistors |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/cr0501543 |journal=Chemical Reviews |language=en |volume=107 |issue=4 |pages=1296–1323 |doi=10.1021/cr0501543 |pmid=17378616 |issn=0009-2665|url-access=subscription }}</ref> She held a [[Gates Cambridge Scholarship]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-01-30 |title=The science of bread - Gates Cambridge |url=https://www.gatescambridge.org/about/news/the-science-of-bread/ |access-date=2022-12-08 |website=Gates Cambridge - |language=EN}}</ref> She was a postdoctoral fellow at the [[Argonne National Laboratory]], based in the Center for Nanoscale Materials.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Three young scientists named postdocs at Argonne {{!}} Argonne National Laboratory |url=https://www.anl.gov/article/three-young-scientists-named-postdocs-at-argonne |access-date=2022-12-08 |website=www.anl.gov |date=2 February 2007 |language=en}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
In 2009, Zaumseil moved to the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Angewandte Phys Chemie |url=https://www.pci.uni-heidelberg.de/apc/staff/zaumseil_cv.html |access-date=2022-12-08 |website=www.pci.uni-heidelberg.de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jana Zaumseil › Technische Fakultät |url=https://www.tf.fau.de/person/jana-zaumseil/ |access-date=2022-12-08 |language=de-DE |archive-date=2022-12-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221208224837/https://www.tf.fau.de/person/jana-zaumseil/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Shortly after arriving in Nuremberg she was awarded the Alfried-Krupp-Förderpreis.<ref name=":0" /> She started to work on plasmic nano antennas that could enhance the performance of [[light-emitting diode]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg: Aktuelles |url=https://www.presse.uni-erlangen.de/2008-2012/infocenter/meldungen/forschung/2012/8/10/127.shtml |access-date=2022-12-08 |website=www.presse.uni-erlangen.de}}</ref> She was made a chair in physical chemistry at [[Heidelberg University]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Angewandte Phys Chemie, J. Zaumseil |url=https://www.pci.uni-heidelberg.de/apc/zaumseil/ |access-date=2022-12-08 |website=www.pci.uni-heidelberg.de}}</ref>

Zaumseil was awarded a [[European Research Council]] Consolidator Grant in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ERC awards €573 million to mid-career researchers from 40 countries |url=https://erc.europa.eu/news/erc-2018-consolidator-grants-results |access-date=2022-12-08 |website=erc.europa.eu |language=en}}</ref>
